record_scope_reconstruction: Mananga road port between South Africa and Eswatini, with a June 29 official closure-status observation and a separate July 1 EFF protest obstruction. They are not merged into an inferred continuous closure.

source_checks.finding: Official SARS notice explicitly lists Mananga closed until further notice as of June 29, 2021; other ports have separate statuses.
Original July 2 report describes the preceding Thursday morning EFF and Swazi protest at Mananga in Nkomazi. References to Matsamo congestion or informal routes do not broaden this record.

sites.coordinate_method: Original OSM node coordinate from independently fetched API JSON
sites.precision: approximate crossing facility area; no survey accuracy claimed
sites.evidence_note: Northern Mananga border-control node, with separate Eswatini controls south of it; border road crossing distinct from parallel railway. Inspected OSM tags: {"access": "permissive", "barrier": "border_control", "description": "7:00-18:00", "name": "Mananga Border Control"}. Geographic evidence only; no historical restriction or current operational status inferred.

phase_decisions.phase_applicability: Official closure-status observation applies to the Mananga road port as a facility. Current phase only: Mananga Port of Entry closure status on June 29, 2021

date_scope_check.qualification_retained:
C7-AF-001-P1: First onset, reopening, movement exceptions and cause are not supplied. Page-wide July 2 date is not a later confirmation. Do not join continuously to the EFF episode.

C7-AF-001-P2: Protest onset is dated to the morning of July 1, 2021 by Sowetan; exact start/end hours and continuity from June 29 remain unestablished.

onset: The June 29 closure supplies no first onset. The separate protest is reported to begin on the morning of July 1, without an exact hour.

endpoint: Neither Mananga observation dates exact restoration; the September 20 announcement provides later permission only.

scope: Movement exceptions to the June 29 closure status are not supplied.

rationale: The June 29 customs closure notice supplies no cause; the July 1 EFF motive cannot be inherited by that earlier observation.

continuity: Continuity between the June 29 closure status and the July 1 EFF obstruction is unestablished.

New source clarification: Sowetan, July 2, explicitly dates the protest shutdown to Thursday morning, July 1. This resolves its onset day, not its exact hour or end; the earlier June 29 observation remains separate. The September 20 tourism-minister announcement lists Mananga open.
date_scope_check.review_limit: No dates, unknown reopenings, duration classifications or continuity assumptions changed by this geographic review.
